subject.title: Inject sibling agent list into session system prompt

question: Should OpenClaw expose sibling-agent roster metadata to model-visible context, and if so should it be a gated `agents_list` extension instead of unconditional system-prompt injection?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but exposing sibling identities, roles, and permission topology changes a model-visible security boundary and product behavior that code inspection alone cannot choose.

options.title: Gated Tool Roster
options.body: Expose only approved sibling metadata for targets already visible to the requester through `agents_list`, with tests and docs for the permission boundary.

options.title: Always-On Prompt Roster
options.body: Inject a compact roster into the system prompt for configured peers, accepting prompt growth and broader model-visible topology exposure.

options.title: Defer Or Reject Core Exposure
options.body: Keep descriptions/config metadata separate and require a broader security design before any prompt or tool roster is added.

recommendation.title: Gated Tool Roster
recommendation.body: Expose only approved sibling metadata for targets already visible to the requester through `agents_list`, with tests and docs for the permission boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: This account introduced `agents_list`, the narrowest likely roster extension point, and has the strongest feature-history signal for the boundary.
